とんかつ とんき 目黒本店.name: Tonkatsu Tonki Meguro Honten
とんかつ とんき 目黒本店.description: A renowned tonkatsu restaurant with a history of nearly 90 years. There is always a line during the day, but turnover is very fast. Their excellent operation is also a must-see: staff ask for your order when you come in, and what you ordered comes out piping hot as soon as you sit down.
とんかつ とんき 目黒本店.reservation: Dinner only, for groups of 4 or more

Nico Chelsea.description: A stylish French bistro tucked away in a back alley of Kagurazaka. It specializes in game meat (gibier). Which game is available depends on that day's supply, but every dish is excellent. You can pick your own wine from the wine cellar, which makes it fun. It is a very popular restaurant, so reservations are essential.

神楽坂 焼鳥 虎.name: Kagurazaka Yakitori Tora
神楽坂 焼鳥 虎.description: A yakitori restaurant on the slightly pricier side for Japan (though still only about $80). The yakitori itself is very good, and the all-you-can-drink plan even includes Yamazaki whisky, so it is great value. It has counter seats only, so going in a small group is recommended. Reservations are essential. Its Tabelog rating is low because it is a new restaurant with few reviews.

純米酒専門 粋酔 日本橋東京店.name: Suisui Nihonbashi Tokyo
純米酒専門 粋酔 日本橋東京店.description: A restaurant where you can drink as much as you like from more than 100 kinds of sake collected from all 47 prefectures of Japan. The range of sake is huge, and if you book a course, you can enjoy it all on an all-you-can-drink basis. The food is decent, so this is a place to go for the sake. Reservations for large groups are also possible.
純米酒専門 粋酔 日本橋東京店.note: It is unclear how well English is supported.

中国家庭料理大連.name: Dairen (Chinese Home Cooking)
中国家庭料理大連.description: A down-to-earth Chinese restaurant that has long been loved by students and office workers. The pan-fried gyoza are very good. It is definitely not the kind of place that appears in travel magazines, so it is recommended if you want to experience a restaurant where local Japanese people go.

フラクタル.name: Fractale
フラクタル.description: One of the top rum bars in Japan. It is so famous that when it comes to rum in Tokyo, almost every bartender will name this bar. Besides rum, it also has beer and whisky. An authentic bar with a calm atmosphere. Its Tabelog rating is low because it has few reviews; on Tabelog, bars generally tend to get low ratings.

Antonic 中目黒店.name: Antonic Nakameguro
Antonic 中目黒店.description: A small gin bar along the Meguro River. It is a cozy place with only a few counter seats, but you can enjoy gins from all over the world. Gin is also sold in the basement.

ボンディ 神保町本店.name: Bondy Jimbocho Honten
ボンディ 神保町本店.description: One of the most famous curry restaurants in Japan, and the pinnacle of Japanese-style curry. Rather than strong spices, it is known for the richness and mellowness that come from slowly simmering apples and onions. To everyone from South Asia: this is curry adapted to Japanese tastes, so please forgive us (lol).

Shanaiya.description: A restaurant serving yakuzen (medicinal) curry. Despite the name, there is no medicine in it; it is a spice curry made with plenty of ingredients that help with things like recovering from fatigue. Reservations are possible at dinner, but at lunchtime it uses a numbered-ticket waiting system. You can also join the waiting list online, but everyone applies when it opens at 10:30, so you need to be ready at that time.

ラ メゾン ダミ.name: La Maison Dami
ラ メゾン ダミ.description: A small French bistro in Meguro. The food is excellent, and the pâté Reo had here was among the best he has ever eaten in his life.

ホルモンまさる.name: Horumon Masaru
ホルモンまさる.description: A Japanese-style BBQ restaurant. Since you grill offal (organ meat), it may not be very familiar to non-Japanese people, but it is very popular among Japanese people. There is not much regular meat, so it is not really recommended for people who do not like offal.

らーめん 谷瀬家.name: Ramen Taniseya
らーめん 谷瀬家.description: In Japan there is a genre called Yokohama Iekei ramen, based on a pork-bone and soy sauce broth. There are many famous shops in this genre in places such as Yokohama and Shin-Sugita, and this is a well-regarded one that is easy to reach from central Tokyo. There are many Yokohama Iekei shops in Tokyo, but quality varies a lot, so be careful. When you hand over your meal ticket, you can choose the noodle firmness, the strength of the soup and the amount of fat. Reo likes "soft, strong, less fat," but most people generally choose firm noodles.

麺家 黒.name: Menya Kuro
麺家 黒.description: A well-regarded Yokohama Iekei shop in Tokyo. For an explanation of Yokohama Iekei, see the description of Ramen Taniseya.

新宿焼肉 牛たんの檸檬 総本店.name: Shinjuku Yakiniku Gyutan no Lemon (Main Shop)
新宿焼肉 牛たんの檸檬 総本店.description: A shop serving thick-cut beef tongue. Many people may be hesitant to eat beef tongue, but its chewy texture is very popular in Japan. We recommend eating it with rice. There are also sister shops besides this one, so please try whichever is easiest to get to.

バー タロウズ.name: Bar Tarrow's
バー タロウズ.description: An authentic bar in Kagurazaka. It has a very large number of whiskies, and the bartender, who has a wealth of experience and knowledge, serves whisky that suits your taste. We don't know how much English he can speak, but he is a wonderful bartender who, we can say for certain, will serve you attentively while using a translation device or similar. Besides whisky, the cocktails are also delicious, and there is a wide variety of rum and other spirits. You can also smoke cigars.

食酒家 岡宮.name: Shokushuka Okamiya
食酒家 岡宮.description: A traditional Japanese izakaya. It is near the house where Reo used to live, and the seafood is very good. A hidden gem loved by locals.
食酒家 岡宮.note: We think they can hardly handle English, so you will need to use translation tools or similar.

らーめん弁慶 門前仲町店.name: Ramen Benkei (Monzen-Nakacho)
らーめん弁慶 門前仲町店.description: There are two flavors: soy sauce and miso. We recommend soy sauce. It is Japanese junk ramen topped with lots of back fat, and the bowls are quite dirty. But the taste is definitely very addictive. Reo ate so much of this ramen that he gained 5 kg. The main shop is in Asakusa, but he has never been there, so he chose this shop.

とんかつ 丸七.name: Tonkatsu Marushichi
とんかつ 丸七.description: In a traditional katsudon, the fried pork is finished by binding it with egg, but the katsudon here is made by preparing the egg and the fried pork separately and placing them on top of the rice. A popular shop that started the so-called "unbound katsudon" boom in Japan. The tonkatsu is very thick, so it has a huge visual impact and looks great in photos. As for the taste, the sauce is quite sweet and the meat is very thick, so it is quite heavy. Recommended for people who love fried food. The line is very long, so you should be in front of the shop when it opens.

おにぎり ぼんご.name: Onigiri Bongo
おにぎり ぼんご.description: The shop that started an onigiri (rice ball) boom in Japan about five years ago. It was originally a renowned shop known only to those in the know, but its social-media-worthy look went viral and it suddenly became extremely popular. It serves only onigiri and miso soup, and the onigiri packed with fillings and the perfectly cooked rice are very delicious. Honestly, we don't know how popular it is now, but we expect a long line. It seems you can reserve take-out orders, but they seem to accept reservations only by phone, so if you want to make a reservation, please ask Reo.

Age.3 ASAKUSA.description: A fried sandwich shop. Fried sandwiches themselves became popular after we came to the US, so honestly we are in the same position as all of you. It seems they have not only fruit sandwiches but also ones you could eat for lunch. Judging from the photos, they look delicious, crispy on the outside with a rich seasoning inside. We have quite a lot of free time in Asakusa, so why not stop by?

きつねや.name: Kitsuneya
きつねや.description: The gyudon (beef bowl) is simple, but the rich seasoning and the tenderly simmered beef are superb. It opens early in the morning for people who work at the market, but because of that it closes early, at 1 PM, so be careful. Tsukiji is on our schedule, but we may not make it before closing time, so if you want to go here, please let the organizers know.

I’m donut ? Omotesando.description: Japan's first fresh doughnuts with a fluffy texture. They went viral about a year ago, and our impression is that young people flocked to eat them. The texture is said to be completely different from American doughnuts, so if you are interested, please try them. There are several shops besides Omotesando, so look for a shop that fits your plans.

牛カツ もと村.name: Gyukatsu Motomura
牛カツ もと村.description: A shop serving fried beef. In Japan, frying pork or chicken is common, but beef was rare. This shop overturned that convention and succeeded. There are shops not only in Tokyo but also in Osaka and Kyoto, so look for the nearest shop according to your plans.

黒毛和牛 壱乃屋 浅草.name: Kuroge Wagyu Ichinoya Asakusa
黒毛和牛 壱乃屋 浅草.description: Wagyu bowls made with genuine Japanese wagyu. They look very beautiful. It is popular with tourists, but from a Japanese point of view the price is a little too high, so its Tabelog rating is low.

Bar CENTIFOLIA.description: A bar extremely focused on looking good on social media. To put it positively, it is the pinnacle of flair bartending, but honestly it goes so far over the top that it makes you laugh. However, the bartender has won a cocktail competition in Japan, and his skill as a bartender is the real thing. If you look at their social media first and are interested, I think it is a place where you can have a special experience.
Bar CENTIFOLIA.reservation: Yes, but there is a puzzling reservation fee

カラクサカレー.name: Kara-Kusa Curry
カラクサカレー.description: Japanese-style curry. The spices come through, but it is more of a curry where you can taste the natural sweetness of vegetables and other ingredients. The shop has also received a Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand. A small shop with only counter seats. It opened about nine years ago, when Reo was working in Kyoto, and he went there often back then. The service getting more careless every year is a bit of a concern.
